'''''Significance''''', established in 2004, is a bimonthly print and digital [[magazine]] published by [[Oxford University Press]] on behalf of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] (RSS), the [[Statistical Society of Australia]] (SSA) and the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA).<ref name=ASA1/> It publishes articles on topics of statistical interest presented at a level suited for a general audience. Articles are reviewed by an editorial board of statistics experts drawn from the three societies.<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/10.1111/(ISSN)1740-9713/homepage/ForAuthors.html |title=Author guidelines|journal=Significance |accessdate=2012-07-13|doi=10.1111/(ISSN)1740-9713|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The founding [[editor-in-chief]] was [[Helen Joyce]].<ref>{{cite news| url=http://commentisfree.guardian.co.uk/helen_joyce/profile.html |location=London |work=The Guardian |title=Helen Joyce|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080110130728/http://commentisfree.guardian.co.uk/helen_joyce/profile.html |archive-date=2008-01-10 }}</ref> The current editor is Anna Britten. ''Significance'' replaced the RSS's journal, [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society#Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series D (The Statistician)|''The Statistician'']].<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1046/j.0039-0526.2003.02062.x |title=Report of the Council for the session 2002-2003. Council Report |year=2003 |journal=[[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series D]]|volume=52 |issue=4 |pages=603–678}}</ref> The magazine also has a [https://significancemagazine.com website].

In addition to ordinary articles in the magazine, additional "virtual issues" (collections of articles on a particular subject area) are made available online.<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/10.1111/(ISSN)1740-9713/homepage/VirtualIssuesPage.html |title=Virtual issues |journal=Significance |accessdate=2010-07-15|doi=10.1111/(ISSN)1740-9713 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In November 2010 the magazine launched its website.<ref>{{cite web|title=Significance Magazine Launches Official Web Site|url=https://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/Significance2010-11-15.pdf|work=Amstat|accessdate=August 19, 2015|date=November 16, 2010}}</ref> Having been launched as a quarterly magazine, ''Significance'' changed to a bimonthly frequency in 2011. In 2020, the regular column 'Dr Fisher's Casebook' was renamed 'the secret statistician', a review prompted by concern about [[Ronald Aylmer Fisher|Fisher's]] views on eugenics (and supported by the lack of salience of the homage to ''[[Dr. Finlay's Casebook]]'').<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1740-9713.01419 |journal=Significance|volume=17|issue=4|author=Tarran, B|title=New look, new structure, new opportunities|page=15|year=2020|doi=10.1111/1740-9713.01419|s2cid=225442448|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Members of either the RSS or the ASA receive the magazine as part of their membership.<ref name=ASA1>{{cite web |url=http://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2010/05/13/significancecoverstorymay1/ |title=Significance Magazine—An ASA and RSS Partnership &#124; Amstat News |publisher=[[American Statistical Association]] |date=2010-05-13 |accessdate=2012-07-13}}</ref> In January 2015, the RSS and ASA decided to make the magazine issues available to the public free of charge a year after their publication.<ref>{{cite web|title=Opening the archives: a significant development|url=http://www.statslife.org.uk/significance/2056-opening-the-archives-a-significant-development|website=www.statslife.org.uk|accessdate=20 February 2015}}</ref>
